title: Staged rollout health bench and decision heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, short-form playbook for running small-to-medium staged launches (cohorts -> region -> full) with an operational "health bench" and simple decision heuristics. Designed for product-ops + eng owners who need deterministic go/no-go gates that balance speed and safety.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target: feature flags, model variant rollouts, non-breaking infra changes, and UX experiments that affect inference path.
- Not for DB schema migrations or infra migrations requiring downtime.
- Expectation: owners instrument metrics and deploy feature flag able to be instantly toggled.

Core health bench metrics (primary gating signals):
- Latency p95 (api_ms_p95) — baseline and cohort. Gate: move forward only if cohort p95 <= 1.3x baseline or absolute p95 < 1200ms.
- Error rate (5xx + model-runtime-errors) — gate: < 0.5% sustained over 30m sliding window, and no >1% single-minute spikes without explanation.
- Throughput (requests/min) — ensure service scales; monitor backpressure and queuing.
- Token cost delta ($/1k tokens) — track unit economics, alert if >20% higher than baseline for >4 hours.
- Quality signal (eval prompt set pass_rate) — if automated eval drops >3 percentage points vs baseline, hold rollout.
- Customer impact signals: conversion/engagement delta, CS tickets — immediate hold on >2 verified customer incidents per cohort.

Decision heuristics (practical):
1) Canary (cohort 0): 1% user traffic or 5 internal users for 2–6 hours. Criteria: no red flags in health bench. If OK -> expand to cohort 1.
2) Cohort 1 (small user group): 5–10% traffic for 12–24 hours. Criteria: metrics stable across two rolling 12-hour windows.
3) Regional expansion: 25% traffic in target region for 24–48 hours. Criteria: regional infra/backpressure stable and global KPIs acceptable.
4) Full rollout: 100% after 48–72 hours of region stability and business KPIs green.

Automatic rollback rules (automated toggles + quick manual escalation):
- Immediate auto-toggle OFF if error rate >2% for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Auto-toggle OFF if p95 becomes >3x baseline or >3000ms for 10 consecutive minutes.
- Manual hold if quality eval delta >5% (product review required).
- If cost delta remains >25% after 6 hours, open cost review and pause expansion.

Escalation path and contacts:
- Triage owner (first responder): oncall-eng -> opens incident channel #prod-rollouts and pings product-ops lead.
- Product owner: Asha Patel (owner) — primary decision for canary progression.
- Engineering lead: Diego Rivera — responsible for hotfix/rollback automation.
- CS liaison: Maya Chen — surface customer complaints and triage tickets.
- Exec notify: if rollback impacts >=5% DAU or persists >6 hours, notify VP Product and SRE director.

Operational checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Feature flag gate implemented and tested (toggle time <10s).
- [ ] Dashboards set up: latency p95, error rate, throughput, cost, eval-quality.
- [ ] Automated alert rules configured in PagerDuty/Alerting.
- [ ] Runbook with toggle commands and rollback steps published in Confluence.
- [ ] Customer success aware; canned messaging drafted for affected cohorts.

Lightweight tracker (copy into a sheet for real runs) - CSV lines below for quick paste:
cohort,owner,start_time,target_traffic,duration_hours,p95_ms,error_rate_pct,cost_delta_pct,quality_delta_pct,status,notes
canary,Asha Patel,2025-02-20T09:00Z,1%,4,220,0.1,2.3,-0.4,in_progress,internal-only
cohort-1,Asha Patel,2025-02-20T13:00Z,7%,24,260,0.3,5.6,-0.9,scheduled,watch cost impact
region-eu,Diego Rivera,2025-02-21T16:00Z,25%,36,310,0.4,3.9,-0.2,planned,provisioned extra capacity

Example mini-sim (decision flow):
- Baseline p95: 180ms. Canary p95 climbs to 360ms (2x) with error rate 0.6% sustained for 30m. Heuristic: p95 >1.3x baseline and sustained error >0.5% -> HOLD. Action: pause expansion, switch canary to internal-only, engage engineering lead to profile tail latency.

Post-mortem and rollback lessons (template):
- Summary: short narrative of what happened.
- Timeline: minute-level events and toggles.
- Root cause analysis: what code/config changed and why.
- Mitigation steps and permanent fixes.
- Playbook updates: adjust thresholds, add observability, or change cohort sizes.

Notes / open questions (to resolve before next run):
- Should cost-alert threshold be dynamic by model family? (e.g., large-models get higher baseline)
- Is the 1.3x p95 multiplier too strict for latencies that are modest in absolute terms?
- Do we want a passive quality guard (slow roll if eval delta between 2–4%) and hard stop >4%?

Quick links and artifacts:
- Quick toggle commands: see Confluence link above.
- Canary dashboard: dashboards/redwood/prod/canary-health (add to linked_artifacts).
- Runbook PR: GITHUB: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/88

Intended next steps:
- Product-ops to run a tabletop exercise (Simulated canary failure) with oncall and eng lead next week.
- Update Confluence playbook with thresholds after feedback.
- Move tracker CSV to shared sheet and add automation for real-time status updates.

-- Asha (product-ops)
